question: A player keeps walking slowly around the court between rallies. What should the umpire do?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: what the umpire should do when a player keeps walking slowly around the court between rallies. The directly on-point sentence is itto-5.11.1 (2) (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26): any unnecessary walk around the court between rallies shall be prevented and, if necessary, Law 16.7 applied. Supporting sentences: itto-5.11.1 (1) (umpire shall ensure players do not deliberately cause delay, Law 16.4); laws-16.4.2 (1) (umpire is sole judge of any delay in play, Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26); laws-16.6.1 (1) (a player shall not deliberately cause delay in play); and the Law 16.7 administration sentences laws-16.7.1.1 (1), laws-16.7.1.2 (1)-(2), laws-16.7.1.3 (1) (warning, fault if previously warned, fault for flagrant offence) plus laws-16.7.2 (1) (report to the Referee, who may disqualify). laws-16.4.1 (1) bears on delay generally but does not answer this part, so it goes in related_sentences.
answer.answer:
Under the Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26 (Clause 5.11.1), the umpire shall ensure that the players do not deliberately cause any delay in play (Law 16.4), and any unnecessary walk around the court between rallies shall be prevented and, if necessary, Law 16.7 shall be applied. Under the Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, the umpire is the sole judge of any delay in play (Law 16.4.2), and a player shall not deliberately cause delay in, or suspension of, play (Law 16.6.1). If Law 16.7 is applied, the umpire administers the breach by issuing a warning to the offending side, or faulting the offending side if previously warned, or faulting the offending side in cases of flagrant offence or breach (Law 16.7.1); and on faulting a side the umpire shall report the offending side immediately to the Referee, who shall have the power to disqualify the offending side from the match (Law 16.7.2).
Law 16.4.1 (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26) states that under no circumstances shall play be delayed to enable a player to recover strength or wind or to receive advice; it concerns delay generally but does not specifically address walking around the court between rallies.

An Umpire is appointed for a match by the Referee (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 2.2). question: When an Instant Review System is in use, what decides a line call challenge?

answer.reasoning: The question has one part: what decides a line call challenge when an Instant Review System is in use. Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), Clause 17.5.2 (1) states that when an IRS is in operation, the system in operation shall decide on any line call challenge, unless it gives an inconsistent or obviously incorrect decision, in which case the Referee instructs the Umpire how to proceed. Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), Clause 2.4.2 (1) repeats that the IRS shall be used to decide any line call challenge. ITTO Clause 5.8.6 (1) adds that the IRS reviews the original decision and indicates the result as "IN", "OUT" or "NO DECISION". These three sentences answer the part. Related but not needed for the answer: ITTO 5.8.10 (1)-(3) details the inconsistent/obviously incorrect procedure (Umpire calls the Referee, Referee instructs how to proceed), and ITTO 8.2 (2) states the challenge result supersedes the original line call.
answer.answer:
When an Instant Review System is in operation, the system in operation itself decides any line call challenge (Laws of Badminton 5.0 (2), in force 2025-04-26, Law 17.5.2; Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26, Clause 2.4.2) — the IRS reviews the original decision and indicates the result of the challenge to the Umpire as either "IN", "OUT" or "NO DECISION" (ITTO Clause 5.8.6). The only exception: unless the system gives an inconsistent or obviously incorrect decision, in which case the Referee shall instruct the Umpire how to proceed (Law 17.5.2).
ITTO Clause 5.8.10 (Instructions to Technical Officials 7.0 (5), in force 2025-04-26) details the exception: if the IRS indicates an inconsistent (e.g. between text and graphic) or obviously incorrect decision, the Umpire calls the Referee before the next rally and the Referee instructs the Umpire how to proceed. ITTO Clause 8.2 (2) adds that the result of a player's challenge where an IRS is in operation supersedes the original line call by the Line Judge.
